Create `solution.py` with lifecycle classes `BaseUnit` and `AuditUnit`.

`BaseUnit(logger=None)` accepts `None` or a `logging.Logger`; invalid values raise `ValueError`. With `None`, use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`. It starts in state `"new"` and stores an internal event list.

Public methods enforce this lifecycle:
- `initialize()` is valid only in `new`, calls `_execute_initialization()`, then changes state to `initialized`.
- `start()` is valid only in `initialized`, calls `_execute_start()`, then changes state to `running`.
- `stop()` is valid only in `running`, calls `_execute_stop()`, then changes state to `stopped`.

Invalid transitions raise `RuntimeError` without calling hooks or changing state. Base hook implementations must append `base:<stage>` to the event list and emit the same text with `logger.debug`.

`AuditUnit` overrides all three hooks. Each override first invokes its superclass hook and then appends and logs `audit:<stage>`. Its `load()` method returns `True` without changing state or events.

Expose read-only properties `state` and `events`; `events` returns an immutable tuple snapshot. Importing the module must not alter global logging configuration. Implement the new API using only the standard library.

Implement a CommonJS module exporting exactly `{ splitEpochNanos, FeedMapper }`.

`splitEpochNanos(value)` accepts a non-negative bigint or a decimal digit string. It returns `{ epochMilliseconds, remainderNanoseconds }`, where the first field is a safe integer and the second is an integer from 0 through 999999. Reject other values, negative values, empty strings, and results whose millisecond component exceeds `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with `TypeError` or `RangeError` as appropriate.

`new FeedMapper(useModernProtocol)` selects one of two telemetry protocols. In the legacy protocol, supported packet kinds are `reading` and `readings`; in the modern protocol, they are `sample` and `samples`. Singular packets contain one measurement in `packet.data`; plural packets contain an array in `packet.data`. A measurement has `{ device, metric, value, atNanos }`, where `device` and `metric` are non-empty strings, `value` is finite, and `atNanos` is accepted by `splitEpochNanos`.

The class must provide:

- `canHandle(packet)`, returning a boolean without throwing for malformed input.
- `getTopics(devices)`, validating an array of non-empty device strings, removing duplicates while retaining first-occurrence order, and returning `legacy/<device>` or `modern/<device>` strings.
- A generator method `map(packet, receivedSequence)` that validates a non-negative safe-integer sequence and the complete packet, then yields one standardized object per measurement in source order. Each result is `{ device, metric, value, timestamp, receivedSequence }`, where `timestamp` is the result of `splitEpochNanos`.

An empty plural packet yields nothing. Invalid packets must throw `TypeError`. The implementation must not mutate input arrays, packets, or measurements, and no returned object may alias a measurement or timestamp object supplied by the caller.

Implement a checked integer expression evaluator in `solution.rs` using only the standard library.

Expose this exact API:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EvalError {
    EmptyExpression,
    UnexpectedToken(usize),
    MissingClosingParen,
    DivisionByZero,
    Overflow,
}

pub fn evaluate(source: &str) -> Result<i64, EvalError>;
```

Support decimal nonnegative integer literals, parentheses, unary `+` and `-`, and binary `+`, `-`, `*`, and `/`. Multiplication and division bind more tightly than addition and subtraction; binary operators associate left-to-right. Unary operators may be chained. ASCII whitespace may occur between tokens. Any other character is invalid, and `UnexpectedToken` contains its byte offset.

Use checked `i64` arithmetic, including literal parsing, negation, and the `i64::MIN / -1` case. Division truncates toward zero. Report `DivisionByZero` when appropriate. An empty or whitespace-only input returns `EmptyExpression`. An opening parenthesis without a matching closing parenthesis returns `MissingClosingParen`. Extra tokens, empty parentheses, missing operands, and unmatched closing parentheses return `UnexpectedToken` at the first offending byte; when an operand is missing at end-of-input, use `source.len()`. The input must not be mutated.

```rust
pub enum ModelType {
    Text,
    Integer,
    Decimal,
    Flag,
    Named(String),

    Dictionary(Box<ModelType>),
}

    pub required: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]

    pub name: String,
    pub properties: Vec<Property>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GenerationError {
    InvalidIdentifier(String),
    DuplicateModel(String),
    DuplicateProperty { model: String, property: String },
    UnknownModel(String),
}

pub fn emit_rust_models(models: &[Model]) -> Result<String, GenerationError>;
```

Requirements:
- Valid identifiers are nonempty ASCII identifiers beginning with a letter or underscore and continuing with letters, digits, or underscores.
- Validate model names, property names, duplicate models, duplicate properties, and every `Named` reference before producing output. A reference may target a model declared later.

- A non-required property wraps its complete mapped type in `Option<...>`.
- Inputs must not be mutated.
- Do not include a `main` function.

Implement parsers for a self-contained packet format in `solution.rs`.

A packet consists of a first line `VERB route`, zero or more attribute lines in `name:value` form, one empty line, and an arbitrary body. Lines and the header/body separator use LF (`\n`) only. The first empty line is always the separator, even if the body contains additional blank lines. LF is the only framing character: a carriage return (`\r`) inside an attribute value is literal data and must be preserved exactly rather than stripped or interpreted as part of CRLF framing.

Expose `Verb` with `Read`, `Write`, `Replace`, and `Remove`; `Packet` with public `verb`, `route`, `attributes: Vec<(String, String)>`, and `payload: Vec<u8>` fields; and `TextPacket` with the same fields except `payload: String`. Expose `ParseError` variants `MissingSeparator`, `InvalidHeaderUtf8`, `InvalidStartLine`, `UnknownVerb`, `InvalidAttribute`, and `InvalidBodyUtf8`.

Implement:
- `pub fn parse_packet(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Packet, ParseError>`.
- `pub fn parse_text_packet(input: &[u8]) -> Result<TextPacket, ParseError>`.

The start line must contain exactly two non-empty space-separated fields. Attribute names must be non-empty; values may be empty and are preserved exactly, including any carriage return. Preserve attribute order and duplicates. Binary bodies may contain any bytes and may be empty. The text parser must reject a non-UTF-8 body. Parsing must not mutate or retain aliases into the input. Provide a new complete implementation without `main`.

Create `solution.rs` implementing notification-rule creation and atomic patching. Expose `Channel` with variants `Email`, `Sms`, and `Dashboard`; `NoticeRule { pub id: u64, pub channels: Vec<Channel>, pub subject_prefix: String, pub expires_after: Option<u32>, pub tags: Option<Vec<String>> }`; `RulePatch { pub expires_after: Option<Option<u32>>, pub tags: Option<Option<Vec<String>>> }`; and `RuleError` with variants `InvalidId`, `NoChannels`, `EmptyPrefix`, `ZeroExpiry`, and `EmptyTag`. `create_rule` accepts an ID, channels, and prefix, validates them, and creates a rule whose optional fields are `None`. ID zero, no channels, or a whitespace-only prefix is invalid; preserve the prefix exactly. `update_rule(&mut NoticeRule, RulePatch)` uses tri-state patch fields: outer `None` preserves the field, `Some(None)` clears it, and `Some(Some(value))` sets it. An expiry of zero or any whitespace-only tag is invalid. Validate the entire proposed result before mutating the rule, so errors leave it byte-for-byte unchanged. Empty tag vectors are valid. `ordered_rules(&[NoticeRule]) -> Vec<&NoticeRule>` returns references sorted by ascending ID, preserving original relative order for duplicate IDs and never mutating the slice. #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
```rust
pub struct ProfileCard {
    pub code: String,

}

pub fn parse_profile_card(input: &str) -> Result<ProfileCard, &'static str>;
```

Each nonblank line must contain exactly one field assignment of the form `key=value`; surrounding ASCII whitespace around the key and value is ignored.
